{{Short description|none}} {{use dmy dates|date=November 2024}} {{Opinion polling for Brazilian presidential elections}} Since the [[2022 Brazilian general election]], polling companies have published surveys tracking national voting intention for the [[2026 Brazilian general election]]. The results of these surveys are listed below in reverse chronological order, and include candidates who frequently polled above 3% and are [[List of political parties in Brazil|registered in a party]], as well as eligible by the [[Superior Electoral Court]] of Brazil. They also include candidates from parties that passed the [[electoral threshold]]{{efn|name="electoral threshold"}} in 2022, and therefore have access to public campaign funding, free radio and television advertising time, and the right to participate in debates. == First round == === Graphical summary === [[Aggregate data]] of voting intention from opinion polling for the presidential election. Each line represents a [[local regression]]. Only prospective candidates and individuals who frequently appear in polls are included. and banker [[Daniel Vorcaro]] — including on the day of his arrest — whose confidentiality had been lifted by Justice [[André Mendonça]]. The messages revealed indications of improper closeness between the two, along with other revelations involving Prosecutor General [[Paulo Gonet]]. In response, on 3 September, Moraes requested that an investigation be opened against Mendonça as part of the [[Inquiry 4781|Fake News Inquiry]], for his handling of the [[Banco Master scandal|Master case investigation]].

The situation escalated on 8 September, when Mendonça ordered the preventive removal of the Federal Police's Director-General, [[Andrei Rodrigues]], alleging that he had been illegally monitored by the PF. The following day, 9 September, Justice [[Flávio Dino]] ordered the immediate reinstatement of Rodrigues, creating a standoff. Later that same day, the Court's president, Justice [[Edson Fachin]], suspended both Mendonça's decision and Dino's, maintaining the status quo until a final ruling, and removed Moraes as rapporteur of the fake news inquiry, taking over the case himself. Fachin also called an extraordinary session for 15 September, at which the full court is expected to rule on the legality of Mendonça's actions, the validity of the evidence obtained from Vorcaro's phone, and the Prosecutor General's Office's request to annul the entire procedure. }} {{efn|name="Free airtime" |Candidates from coalitions that include parties which passed the electoral threshold in 2022 are entitled to free advertisement on television and radio from 28 August to 1 October 2026.
